current.text: Experts rank him the number one pick in head-to-head categories leagues and would take him first overall, ahead of Wembanyama.
He has the tightest range of outcomes in round one. Best case is 1st and worst case is 3rd.
In an auction, take him if the room lets him sit near 55 USD. That frees about 20 USD for other players.
He is projected for over 30 percent usage.
Expect about 35 minutes per game again. More regression is not a big worry.
He had the fewest potential assists among the league's assist leaders last season.
His assists could drop to about 10.1 per game if his teammates' shooting evens out.
He can become a free agent after this season.
He is expected to stay in Denver all season and re-sign, although he has not been happy for two years.
Denver plays 43 games through March 28, one below the maximum. It has only 14 back-to-backs, one of the lowest counts in the league.
He plays four games in the week starting March 15, which is fantasy playoff week 20.
Denver is not expected to rest him on purpose.
He has no injury now, and Denver is fairly healthy going into the season.

durable.text: He has been the best fantasy player of the last five or six years and has finished number one in both category and points leagues.
He is a league outlier in FG%, points, rebounds and assists. His high FG% comes on big volume, so it lifts a team's FG% clearly.
Most of his extra value comes from giving both rebounds and assists, two categories that rarely come together.
Turnovers are his one clearly weak category. He commits a lot of them, even for a center.
Threes, blocks and free throws are his relative weak spots, but none of them is a real weakness.
He had a hamstring injury two seasons ago and a somewhat fluky knee injury last season, which cost him a lot of games.
At 31 he is getting slightly less durable, but experts are not worried about his health.
He gets more tired on defense in the middle of the season than he admits.

note: He is the consensus number one pick on both sites, but the prices disagree: Yahoo values him at 61 USD with a 71 USD average cost, ESPN at 68 USD with an 82 USD average cost, and our league paid 87 USD last season. Expect him to go for 75 to 90 USD here. Any price near 55 to 60 USD is a steal. He fits any build, and punt TO teams lose least from his 3.4 turnovers. Early in the season, check that his knee is fine, that he plays about 35 minutes, and whether his assists hold near 10 per game.
